items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines statement of account.
o: an amount paid in one period that relates to a later period
an estimate of the receivables that may not be collected, charged against profit
a document sent to a customer listing the transactions and the balance due
the amount a trader pays to acquire goods for resale
items.s: statement of account: a document sent to a customer listing the transactions and the balance due. The other options describe cost price, provision for doubtful debts, prepaid expense.

items.q: Which of the following best describes bad debt?
o: a schedule of ledger balances drawn up to test the arithmetic equality of debits and credits
money received for a debt that had earlier been written off
a receivable that has proved irrecoverable and is written off
the cost of the goods bought for resale during the period
items.s: bad debt: a receivable that has proved irrecoverable and is written off. The other options describe trial balance, purchases, bad debt recovered.

items.q: compensating error may be defined as
o: a pair of errors that cancel each other so that the trial balance still agrees
a resource owned or controlled by the business that has a money value
an estimate of the receivables that may not be collected, charged against profit
a credit allowed to a partner as a return on the capital he has invested
items.s: compensating error: a pair of errors that cancel each other so that the trial balance still agrees. The other options describe provision for doubtful debts, interest on capital, asset.

items.q: accrued expense may be defined as
o: an expense that has been incurred but not paid by the end of the period
the fixed face value printed on a share certificate
the cost of an asset less its estimated residual value
the method that writes off an equal amount of the depreciable cost in each year
items.s: accrued expense: an expense that has been incurred but not paid by the end of the period. The other options describe nominal value, depreciable cost, straight line depreciation.

items.q: payables control account may be defined as
o: a temporary account that holds the difference on a trial balance until the error is traced
a summary account of the total owed to credit suppliers, checked against the purchases ledger
money received for a debt that had earlier been written off
the total depreciation charged on an asset since it was acquired
items.s: payables control account: a summary account of the total owed to credit suppliers, checked against the purchases ledger. The other options describe bad debt recovered, accumulated depreciation, suspense account.

items.q: Which of the following best describes prepaid expense?
o: the running costs of the business such as rent, wages and electricity
an entry on the left side of an account that increases an asset or an expense
the amount an asset is expected to fetch at the end of its useful life
an amount paid in one period that relates to a later period
items.s: prepaid expense: an amount paid in one period that relates to a later period. The other options describe residual value, operating expenses, debit entry.

items.q: All of the following belong to Gross and net profit EXCEPT
o: net profit
gross profit
turnover
debit entry
items.s: Every other option belongs to Gross and net profit. “debit entry” belongs to Double entry bookkeeping, not Gross and net profit.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method that writes off an equal amount of the depreciable cost in each year”?
o: depreciable cost
useful life
residual value
straight line depreciation
items.s: straight line depreciation is the method that writes off an equal amount of the depreciable cost in each year.

items.q: The statement “the amount an asset is expected to fetch at the end of its useful life” describes which of the following?
o: straight line depreciation
depreciable cost
useful life
residual value
items.s: residual value is the amount an asset is expected to fetch at the end of its useful life.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines prudence convention?
o: a document sent to a customer listing the transactions and the balance due
the practice of providing for expected losses as soon as they are foreseen
the fixed face value printed on a share certificate
capital raised by issuing shares that carry the residual risk and reward of the company
items.s: prudence convention: the practice of providing for expected losses as soon as they are foreseen. The other options describe ordinary share capital, nominal value, statement of account.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines credit note?
o: the method that writes off an equal amount of the depreciable cost in each year
the amount by which one side of an account exceeds the other side
a document sent to a customer to reduce the amount invoiced for goods returned
an expense that has been incurred but not paid by the end of the period
items.s: credit note: a document sent to a customer to reduce the amount invoiced for goods returned. The other options describe straight line depreciation, accrued expense, account balance.

items.q: prepaid expense may be defined as

the rule that expenses are set against the income of the period they helped to earn
an amount paid in one period that relates to a later period
the amount a trader pays to acquire goods for resale
items.s: prepaid expense: an amount paid in one period that relates to a later period. The other options describe partners' current account, matching principle, cost price.

items.q: operating expenses may be defined as

the running costs of the business such as rent, wages and electricity
an entry on the left side of an account that increases an asset or an expense
the amount a trader pays to acquire goods for resale
items.s: operating expenses: the running costs of the business such as rent, wages and electricity. The other options describe cost price, asset, debit entry.

items.q: Which term is described by “the amount an asset is expected to fetch at the end of its useful life”?

depreciable cost
straight line depreciation
residual value
items.s: residual value is the amount an asset is expected to fetch at the end of its useful life.

items.q: bank reconciliation statement may be defined as

the relationship that the assets of a business equal its capital plus its liabilities
the interest of the owner in the business, measured as assets less liabilities
a statement that reconciles the cash book balance with the balance on the bank statement
items.s: bank reconciliation statement: a statement that reconciles the cash book balance with the balance on the bank statement. The other options describe owner's capital, statement of account, accounting equation.

items.q: Which term is described by “an entry on the left side of an account that increases an asset or an expense”?
o: debit entry
contra entry
double entry principle
credit entry
items.s: debit entry is an entry on the left side of an account that increases an asset or an expense.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines trial balance?
o: money received for a debt that had earlier been written off
an expense that has been incurred but not paid by the end of the period
a schedule of ledger balances drawn up to test the arithmetic equality of debits and credits
a cheque returned unpaid by the bank of the customer who issued it
items.s: trial balance: a schedule of ledger balances drawn up to test the arithmetic equality of debits and credits. The other options describe dishonoured cheque, accrued expense, bad debt recovered.

items.q: mark-up may be defined as
o: the cost of an asset less its estimated residual value
the value of the goods held by the business at the beginning of the period
the profit of a trader expressed as a percentage of the cost price
an entry that transfers an amount between two accounts, such as cash paid into the bank
items.s: mark-up: the profit of a trader expressed as a percentage of the cost price. The other options describe contra entry, depreciable cost, opening stock.

items.q: The statement “a schedule of ledger balances drawn up to test the arithmetic equality of debits and credits” describes which of the following?
o: trial balance
account balance
suspense account
compensating error
items.s: trial balance is a schedule of ledger balances drawn up to test the arithmetic equality of debits and credits.

a business owned by two or more persons who share profits in an agreed ratio
the agreed proportion in which the partners divide the profits of the firm
the relationship that the assets of a business equal its capital plus its liabilities
items.s: accounting equation: the relationship that the assets of a business equal its capital plus its liabilities. The other options describe profit sharing ratio, partnership, liability.

items.q: Which of the following best describes contra entry?
o: an estimate of the receivables that may not be collected, charged against profit
a summary account of the total owed to credit suppliers, checked against the purchases ledger
an entry that transfers an amount between two accounts, such as cash paid into the bank
the rule that expenses are set against the income of the period they helped to earn
items.s: contra entry: an entry that transfers an amount between two accounts, such as cash paid into the bank. The other options describe matching principle, provision for doubtful debts, payables control account.

items.q: Which term is described by “the cost of an asset less the depreciation charged on it to date”?
o: accumulated depreciation
book value
accelerated charge
reducing balance depreciation
items.s: book value is the cost of an asset less the depreciation charged on it to date.

items.q: Which of the following best describes compensating error?

the amount an asset is expected to fetch at the end of its useful life
an amount owed by the business to a party outside the business
a lodgement made by the business but not yet credited by the bank
items.s: compensating error: a pair of errors that cancel each other so that the trial balance still agrees. The other options describe uncredited deposit, residual value, liability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines share premium.

a receivable that has proved irrecoverable and is written off
the excess of the amount received on shares over their nominal value
the cost of the goods bought for resale during the period
items.s: share premium: the excess of the amount received on shares over their nominal value. The other options describe purchases, bad debt, profit sharing ratio.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines gross profit.

the excess of sales revenue over the cost of the goods sold
a pair of errors that cancel each other so that the trial balance still agrees

items.q: Which of the following best describes payables control account?

the interest of the owner in the business, measured as assets less liabilities
a cheque returned unpaid by the bank of the customer who issued it
a summary account of the total owed to credit suppliers, checked against the purchases ledger

the value of the goods held by the business at the beginning of the period

the account that records each partner's share of profit, drawings and interest
gross profit expressed as a percentage of sales

a depreciation pattern in which the charge is larger in the early years of the life of the asset
a credit allowed to a partner as a return on the capital he has invested

an entry on the left side of an account that increases an asset or an expense

items.q: A receivables control account has an opening debit balance of 150000 naira. Credit sales were 620000 naira, cash received from customers was 705000 naira and sales returns were 25000 naira. What is the closing balance?

items.q: Rent paid during the year was 300000 naira. Rent accrued at the beginning of the year was 10000 naira and rent accrued at the end of the year was 55000 naira. What is the rent expense for the year?

items.q: A company issued 100000 ordinary shares of nominal value 1 naira each at 2 naira each. What is the total share premium received?

items.q: Operating profit was 210000 naira and capital employed was 1200000 naira. What is the return on capital employed in percent?
items.s: Return on capital employed = operating profit/capital employed x 100 = 210000/1200000 x 100 = 17.5 percent.

items.q: The total assets of a firm are 460000 naira and its capital is 340000 naira. What is the total of its liabilities?

items.q: A machine costing 500000 naira has a residual value of 40000 naira and a useful life of 8 years. What is the annual straight line depreciation charge?
items.s: Straight line charge = (cost - residual value)/life = (500000 - 40000)/8 = 57500 naira per year.

items.q: An asset is bought for 600000 naira and depreciated at 15 percent per annum on the reducing balance. What is the depreciation charge for the first year?
items.s: First year charge = cost x rate = 600000 x 15/100 = 90000 naira.

items.q: A vehicle costing 250000 naira is depreciated at 25 percent per annum on the reducing balance. What is its net book value at the end of 3 years?
items.s: Net book value = cost x (1 - rate/100)^years = 250000 x (1 - 25/100)^3 = 105468.75 naira.
